cues.show: You with the guitar, the drill's tab on screen.
cues.say: This drill uses two fingers on one string. You pick the first note, and after that the fingers make every note by themselves.

cues.show: Fretting hand close up: one hammer-on, slowly.
cues.say: This is a hammer-on. One finger holds a note, and the next finger comes down hard just behind its fret, like a small hammer. You don't pick it.

cues.show: Fretting hand close up: one pull-off, slowly.
cues.say: This is a pull-off. The finger leaves the string by flicking it a little to the side, so the lower note rings. The finger under it has to be down already.

cues.show: Press the Play button and play along.
cues.say: Press the Play button below to start the metronome and the notes, one note on each beat.

cues.show: Press the Play button and play along.
cues.say: Pick once, then hammer on and pull off in time with it.

cues.show: Stop and shake the hand out.
cues.say: _Stop and rest as soon as your hand feels tight._

cues.show: Stop and shake the hand out.
cues.say: Practice until the two notes are as loud as each other.

cues.show: Play the trill on a thicker string, then with another pair of fingers.
cues.say: Try things with it. Play the same two fingers on another string: the thick strings need a harder hammer.

cues.show: Play the trill on a thicker string, then with another pair of fingers.
cues.say: Try another pair of fingers and notice which pair is weaker.

cues.show: Play the trill on a thicker string, then with another pair of fingers.
cues.say: Then play it without picking at all, starting with a hammer-on.
